trial.title: Linzhi Jianghuang Fufang Huoxue Anshen Capsule for Non-alcoholic Fatty Liver

endpoints.description: Primary endpoint will be the change in liver fat content from baseline, as measured by Magnetic Resonance Imaging-Proton Density Fat Fraction (MRI-PDFF) after 24 weeks of treatment.
Changes in liver fat content from baseline, as measured by Liverscan.
Changes in liver stiffness from baseline, as measured by Liverscan.
Changes in metabolic parameter (e.g., insulin resistance) from baseline to the end of 24 weeks of treatment.
Changes in anthropometric parameter (e.g., Body Mass Index) from baseline.
Change in Fatty Liver Index (FLI) score from baseline to the end of 24 weeks of treatment. It ranges from 0 to 100. A FLI \< 30 can be used to rule out and a FLI ≥ 60 to rule in hepatic steatosis.

Change in Hepatic Steatosis Index (HSI) score from baseline to the end of 24 weeks of treatment. The result is expressed on a scale from 0 to 100, with values \<30 ruling out fatty liver, whereas values \>36 confirm its presence.
Change in Fibrosis-4 Index (FIB-4) score from baseline to the end of 24 weeks of treatment. A FIB-4 score below 1.30 generally indicates a low likelihood of liver fibrosis.

Changes in the Chronic Liver Disease Questionnaire-Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease (CLDQ-NAFLD) score. Each item is scored on a 7-point Likert scale, and the total score is the average of the 6 domain scores, with higher scores indicating better quality of life.

Sleep quality will be assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), a 19-item instrument whose items generate 7 component scores that are summed into a global score ranging from 0 to 21, with higher scores indicating poorer sleep quality.

Fatigue will be assessed using the Chalder Fatigue Questionnaire (CFQ-11), an 11-item instrument whose scores are summed into a total score ranging from 0 to 33, with higher scores indicating greater fatigue.
Adverse events (AEs) occurring from the participant's enrollment to the end of the trial and any abnormal changes in laboratory parameters will be recorded.

analysis_trace.finding: Phase 2 RCT of LJF (Linzhi Jianghuang Fufang Huoxue Anshen Capsule), a 5-herb TCM formula (Salviae Miltiorrhizae, Puerariae Lobatae, etc.) for MAFLD/NAFLD. Triple-blind, parallel design, 180 participants, 24-week treatment. Primary endpoint: MRI-PDFF change. Status: NOT_YET_RECRUITING; expected completion 2028-07-01.

Adults 18-65 with MAFLD (MRI-PDFF ≥10%, liver stiffness <7.3 kPa), metabolic risk factors, TCM Phlegm-Stasis pattern. Excludes significant fibrosis, diabetes with HbA1c ≥9.5%, insulin use, recent weight change >5%. Early-stage population amenable to medical intervention.

TCM formula with 'huoxue anshen' (blood-activating, mind-calming) properties. Key herbs: Danshen (Salvia miltiorrhiza) improves metabolic targets (JNK, SREBP-1c, PPARs) and steatosis; Pueraria lobata (kudzu) improves insulin resistance, lipid metabolism, oxidative stress. Multi-target metabolic modulation.

Primary: MRI-PDFF (gold standard for liver fat quantification). Secondary: Liverscan (CAP/LSM), metabolic parameters, anthropometrics, FLI/HSI/FIB-4 scores, PROs (CLDQ-NAFLD, PSQI, CFQ-11), safety. Mix of objective imaging, biomarkers, and patient-reported outcomes.

Systematic reviews (53 RCTs, n=5997) show TCMs improve liver enzymes, lipids, and B-ultrasound resolution vs placebo, but methodological quality is low. Danshen specifically shows metabolic target modulation. No direct evidence for LJF formula. Qushi Huayu trial (24 weeks) showed liver fat reduction via transient elastography. Evidence supports directional benefit but precise effect sizes uncertain.

TCM herbal formulas generally well-tolerated with mild, reversible GI adverse effects. No serious safety signals in prior NAFLD RCTs. 24-week exposure duration is moderate. Herb-drug interaction potential exists but trial excludes unstable medications.

1) No prior clinical data for this specific LJF formula; 2) Low methodological quality of TCM NAFLD trials limits confidence; 3) Recruitment challenges for TCM trials; 4) Placebo response in lifestyle-dependent conditions; 5) MRI-PDFF as primary requires significant fat reduction to demonstrate efficacy.

No direct clinical trial results for LJF formula. No published efficacy data for this specific 5-herb combination. No MRI-PDFF data from comparable TCM trials. Mechanistic evidence from component herbs must be extrapolated.
